subject: Private VPC failover & responsibility clauses — evidence + proposed appendix
messages:
From: Arjun Mehta <arjun@blueharbor.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Lowe <samantha.lowe@blueharbor.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: carveout for customer-controlled transit & evidence request

Vanessa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re getting legal and netops aligned on the Private deployment and there’s one open item blocking procurement: we need a narrow SLA appendix that acknowledges BlueHarbor controls the MPLS transit and on-prem edge routers for our colocations. Specifically: when packet drops or latency tails are due to our transit or colo-SP routing, we want a clear exception so Redwoods’ latency SLOs aren’t used to trigger credits.

Two asks from our side:
- Acceptance of a limited carveout that attributes tail latency to customer-managed transit when BlueHarbor provides evidence (BGP flow logs, packet captures, or sFlow summaries) showing packet loss or egress queues in our edge.
- A concrete list of observability signals Redwood requires for attribution, and an operational SLA for how Redwood will investigate (turnaround and remediation steps).

Attached: a zip with sample pcap/flow snippets from a recent incident. Happy to hop on a quick call if needed.

—Arjun
Arjun Mehta
Head of Infrastructure, BlueHarbor Systems

Subject: Re: Request: carveout for customer-controlled transit & evidence request

Arjun —

Thanks for the attachment and the clear asks. Short answer: we can accept a narrowly scoped exception for customer-managed transit, but we need (1) a reproducible evidence protocol and (2) an operational playbook that ensures attribution is verifiable and not used to avoid uptime obligations broadly.

Proposed next steps from our side:
1) Karthik and I will draft a short appendix that:
   - Limits carveouts to third-party transit / on-prem SW/hardware faults only (explicitly excludes Redwood runtime faults like KV cache corruption or model-serving crashes).
   - Requires BlueHarbor to produce one of the following evidentiary items within 72 hours of an incident: BGP route-change export with timestamps, sFlow/NetFlow samples showing egress drops, or synchronized pcap snippets with NTP-aligned timestamps.
2) Product Ops (Priyom) will document the observability signals we need from customer side and the Redwood signals we will capture (per-request traces, edge egress counters, kernel tx-drop counters).
3) Naomi will run the evidence you sent through our incident parsing tool to validate it’s sufficient for attribution.

If that sounds workable I’ll attach a draft appendix for review by EOW. If you prefer a call we can do 30m tomorrow at 10am PT.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: carveout for customer-controlled transit & evidence request

Arjun/Vanessa —

I took a look at the zip. High level legal/contract guidance below (draft language to follow in the docx):

- Scope: The exception should be limited to third-party transit and on-prem edge equipment/performance issues where the customer can produce time-aligned evidence that correlates to Redwood request timestamps. We do not want a broad "no-credit" clause.
- Evidence standard: We propose a three-tier evidence model (one required):
   * Tier A: Synchronized packet capture excerpts (pcap) with NTP-synced timestamps + corroborating border router counters showing drops.
   * Tier B: Border router NetFlow/sFlow exports showing sustained egress drops or abnormal retransmit rates for the affected 5-minute window.
   * Tier C: BGP route-change dump where route flaps align with the incident window and other infra (CDN/backbone) ruled out.
- Investigation timetable: Redwood will acknowledge incident submission within 8 hours and provide preliminary attribution findings within 48 hours; final findings within 7 calendar days unless the incident is escalated.
- Graceful fallback: If evidence is inconclusive, we propose a joint post-incident review and temporary remediation credits at a reduced rate (e.g., 25% of the standard credit), rather than a full denial. This reduces finger-pointing while protecting customer trust.

I'll attach a redlined appendix for Vanessa to include in the contract pack.

—Karthik Iyer
Dir., Solutions & Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: carveout for customer-controlled transit & evidence request

Arjun —

Quick operational note and attached proposed appendix (proposed-sla-appendix-diff.docx). We ran the sample pcaps through our parser: the captures are useful but we need clearer NTP alignment and a 1s-precision mapping from Redwood request IDs to packet timestamps. Practically speaking, here’s what we’ll need ongoing to accept attribution claims without manual forensics: 

- Required signals from BlueHarbor for any claim:
  - NetFlow/sFlow export for the 30m window surrounding incident (CSV with timestamps).
  - Router interface counters (tx/err/drop) for the same window.
  - Optional but recommended: 10s pcap sample with NTP-synced timestamps for the affected flows.

- What Redwood will record automatically:
  - Per-request trace id, request start/end timestamp, egress edge node id, and per-stage latency histograms.
  - If present, kernel tx-drop and NIC error counters on our edge proxies.

- Investigation SLA: Incident packet + flow evidence submitted by customer within 72 hours -> Redwood preliminary attribution in 48 hours, final report in 7 days. If customer cannot provide required signals within 72 hours, we will proceed with Redwood-side analysis and reserve the right to apply standard uptime/latency SLOs.

If that works, please confirm and we’ll circulate the redline to your legal. Happy to host a joint ops run-through to make sure the evidence export is reproducible in your environment.

—Priyom Das
Product Operations, Redwood Inference
